page.title: Inflammatory bowel disease
about: Symptoms of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) include diarrhoea that lasts longer than 4 weeks, tummy pain, and blood or mucus in your poo.

lines.text: The main symptoms of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) can include:
diarrhoea that lasts longer than 4 weeks
tummy pain
blood or mucus (clear slime) in your poo
bleeding from your bottom
feeling tired all the time
losing weight without trying

cards.headline: Call 999 or go to A&E if:

lines.text: you have severe tummy pain
you're bleeding non-stop from your bottom
there's a lot of blood or you see large blood clots when you poo
you're vomiting blood or poo, or your sick looks like coffee grounds or soil
There are 3 main types of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD).
They affect different parts of your digestive system but the symptoms and treatment are often similar.
Treatment for inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) will depend on your symptoms. If you're very unwell, you may need to be treated in hospital.
Treatments may include:
medicines to help ease your symptoms, such as steroids, and other medicines that can help keep your symptoms under control
surgery to remove part of your bowel, if your symptoms are severe
It's not clear what causes inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). It's thought it happens when your immune system attacks your bowel, which causes it to become inflamed (swollen).
You're more likely to get IBD if one of your close relatives has it, such as one of your parents, siblings or grandparents.

cards.headline: Help and support for inflammatory bowel disease (IBD)

lines.text: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) can be difficult to live with both physically and emotionally.
As well as support from your doctor and care team, there are national charities that can offer information, help and support.
You may find it helpful to get support from other people with IBD, either at a local support group or online.
You can also refer yourself directly to an NHS talking therapies service without needing a referral from a GP.
Crohn's and Colitis UK provides help and support for people living with IBD.
